name: Anarcho-Capitalism
summary: Anarcho-capitalism holds that the state, a compulsory monopoly of force funded by taxation, should be abolished and its functions, including courts, police and defense, provided by competing private firms in a market society. It rests on self-ownership, property acquired by labor and the non-aggression principle, which forbids initiating force or fraud. Adherents accept wage labor, private ownership of industry and free markets, and most regard taxation as theft and war as state mass murder.
scope: The mainstream Rothbardian strand: Murray Rothbard (For a New Liberty, The Ethics of Liberty), with Hans-Hermann Hoppe, David Friedman, the Tannehills and Molinari as documented in the Wikipedia article. Minarchist libertarianism and individualist anarchism of Tucker and Spooner are excluded; left-Rothbardian and Friedmanite consequentialist variants are noted but not followed, and answers where adherents split (immigration, culture) are set to neutral.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Health care is among the services anarcho-capitalists would privatize, with those unable to pay relying on charity and mutual aid rather than state guarantees.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage labor is treated as a voluntary contract, so a legally set wage floor is an interference the ideology rejects.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Rothbard argued that state services are inefficient because they lack market pricing, and the ideology would give markets every function the state performs.

public-ownership.rationale: State property is regarded as illegitimate or stolen and the aim is to return it to private owners, not to expand it.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation of anyone is described as theft on a massive scale, so higher taxes on the wealthy are rejected along with the rest.

unions-good.rationale: Voluntary unions are permitted, but adherents are generally skeptical of unions and of the state privileges they gained; views vary.

property-fundamental.rationale: Original appropriation and self-ownership make private property the foundation of the whole system, and it may not be overridden.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation is state coercion; adherents would rely on competition, reputation and private adjudication to restrain firms.

cut-welfare.rationale: State welfare is financed by taxation and would be abolished, with help coming from charity and mutual aid.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers may form cooperatives voluntarily, but wage labor and ownership by investors are accepted as legitimate, so no collective ownership is sought.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Force may be used only against those who have committed aggression, so drug use between consenting adults is not a crime.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Physical force is justified only against aggressors, and speech is not aggression, so laws restricting it are rejected.

strong-leader.rationale: The ideology wants to abolish the state, so concentrating power in a leader is the opposite of its aim.

limit-guns.rationale: Defense is a private matter, and strict limits on ownership would use force against people who have not been convicted of aggression.

empower-police-military.rationale: Public police and military are monopolies to be replaced by competing private defense, not funded further.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Rothbard calls prostitution a voluntary sale of labor that government has no right to prohibit or restrict.

decide-locally.rationale: The ideology favors decentralization down to individual choice and voluntary secession, though it aims at no state at all rather than local government.

rehabilitation.rationale: Justice centers on restitution to victims and, in Rothbard's version, proportionate punishment, not on rehabilitation as a state program.

traditional-family.rationale: Adherents split: Hoppe's strand defends traditional norms while Rothbard's emphasis on personal liberty and the left-Rothbardian strand do not.

abortion-legal.rationale: Rothbard defends the absolute right of a woman to own her own body and therefore to abortion, though some adherents dissent.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The ideology takes no position on this question and adherents differ.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The ideology rejects the nation-state, and adherents split between cultural conservatives such as Hoppe and cosmopolitan libertarians.

gradual-change.rationale: Adherents seek to abolish the state, not conserve its institutions, though Rothbard preferred peaceful, voluntary means, so change is not necessarily rapid.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Adherents split: Hoppe argues open borders is not a libertarian principle and favors owner-controlled entry, while others favor free movement.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: International bodies are further states and further monopolies of coercion, so giving them more power is rejected.

free-trade.rationale: Voluntary exchange is central, and tariffs and trade controls are state interference; stated mostly by implication from market principles.

nation-first.rationale: The ideology is cosmopolitan in outlook and abolishes the state, so no state pursues national interest, but adherents differ.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: War is described as mass murder on a scale private police could never reach, so state military interventions are rejected.

open-borders.rationale: Under private property there are no national borders to open; adherents split over whether owners should admit all comers, as Hoppe's critique of open borders shows.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Adherents hold that private ownership and private adjudication internalize externalities, and they reject large government programs.

revolution-justified.rationale: Rothbard considered the American Revolution a just war but thought violent revolution generally counterproductive, preferring peaceful secession.

central-planning.rationale: Central planning lacks market prices, which Rothbard and other adherents say makes it inefficient and coercive.

socialized-markets.rationale: Adherents accept markets under any voluntary ownership, but regard public ownership as theft and so do not accept the condition set.

land-value-tax.rationale: Taxation is theft in the ideology, and geolibertarian arguments that land cannot be privately owned are among its criticisms.

tax-inheritance.rationale: All taxation is regarded as theft, and inheritance is a voluntary transfer of private property.

basic-income.rationale: A state-funded transfer would be financed by taxation, which the ideology regards as theft.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of the economy is rejected as inefficient and coercive.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wage labor and market money are accepted as voluntary arrangements and would not be abolished.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies fixing wages and prices would be coercive, and the ideology leaves these to voluntary contract.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hoppe judges monarchy the lesser evil to democracy, but the ideology rejects any state, so most adherents do not call it legitimate.

democracy-best.rationale: Hoppe's Democracy: The God That Failed argues democracy drives state growth, and Rothbard held the state illegitimate whatever its form.

workers-councils.rationale: The ideology rejects political power of any kind as the basis of order, whoever holds it.

right-to-secede.rationale: Rothbard preferred voluntary secession and Hoppe expects secession to multiply jurisdictions, and secession down to the individual is the logical end.

natural-rulers.rationale: The ideology holds that no one has a right to rule others, and the state is the object of its critique.

political-violence-never.rationale: The non-aggression principle permits force in defense, and Rothbard accepted some wars and rebellions as just.

war-builds-character.rationale: War is described as mass murder carried out by the state and not as ennobling.

separate-church-state.rationale: There is no state in the ideal, so no church-state link exists, and religion is left to voluntary association.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Rothbard grounded law in a libertarian code from natural law, and private courts and shared reason rather than scripture would supply it.

private-courts-defense.rationale: This is the central institutional claim, with competing private courts, police firms and defense agencies replacing public ones.

military-superiority.rationale: State militaries are rejected in favor of private defense, and war is attacked as mass murder.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The ideology does not organize society by ethnic nation, though Hoppe's strand favors homogeneous voluntary communities.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rothbard's Egalitarianism as a Revolt Against Nature rejects equality of outcomes, and he said egalitarianism needs a state.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Land belongs to those who first mix their labor with it, which could support some claims but not collective authority; adherents are not settled.

civilizational-union.rationale: Uniting states is the opposite of abolishing them, and the ideology rejects political unions of any kind.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Adherents see self-ownership and trade as legitimate pursuit of one's ends, though not all defend egoism as an ethic.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rights, held by individuals and rooted in self-ownership, come first and community duties are only voluntary.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Adherents use private ownership to protect nature but have no common view on intrinsic value.

limit-population.rationale: Rothbard opposes compulsory birth control, so state limits on population growth are rejected.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Adherents are generally enthusiastic about market-driven technology, but the ideology has no stated position on speeding up disruption.

restore-past-order.rationale: The ideology wants a stateless future rather than a restoration, though Hoppe's strand has traditionalist leanings.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Rothbard grounded the ideology in natural-law rights and the non-aggression principle as moral absolutes, not in case-by-case results.

means-match-ends.rationale: Rothbard stresses persuading rather than compelling, in keeping with a voluntary society.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Specialization and exchange are the basis of the market order the ideology defends.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution follows voluntary exchange and property, not need, apart from voluntary charity.

production-for-use.rationale: Profit-driven production under private ownership is the center of the economic system.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Wage labor and profit are held to arise from voluntary contracts and not exploitation, a view most anarchists criticize.

collective-farming.rationale: Private ownership of land by original appropriation is basic to the theory.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Rothbard blamed states for war and big business's reliance on state favor, not capitalism as such.

taxation-theft.rationale: Rothbard asks whether taxation is theft on a massive scale, and the position is central to the ideology.

harm-principle.rationale: Rothbard holds that force is justified only to restrain force, similar to the harm principle but without granting the state the power.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The ideology is built on individual self-ownership and negative rights, and it does not recognize group rights.

conscription.rationale: Conscription is described as mass enslavement.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Adherents stress exit, secession and competing jurisdictions over voting, and Hoppe argues democracy fails.

state-as-business.rationale: The idea of customers who can leave matches some adherents' views of competing providers, but the ideology rejects the state altogether.

positive-liberty.rationale: Strict Rothbardians accept negative rights and reject positive rights, and critics note that their idea of freedom is purely negative.

media-academia-power.rationale: Rothbard criticized court intellectuals as allies of the state but the ideology has no position on this claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Rothbard defended natural differences in his egalitarianism essay, but the ideology as such takes no position on race and adherents differ.

organic-representation.rationale: Any representation scheme gives authority to a state, which the ideology rejects.

national-rebirth.rationale: The ideology does not center on nations, and a radical national rebirth would require state mobilization.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Wars of expansion are state aggression, and the ideology treats war as mass murder.

bound-labor.rationale: Most adherents reject feudal bondage as coercion, but Block and others defend voluntary slavery contracts, so rejection is the documented majority view rather than settled.

universal-morality.rationale: Rothbard and the Tannehills required a shared ethical basis for law, though Friedman does not, so adherents differ.

single-common-good.rationale: The ideology holds that no single end is imposed and that competing providers of law serve differing preferences.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Firms are governed by their owners and by voluntary contract, not by votes imposed on them.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education would be fully privatized, and vouchers still rest on taxation, though some adherents accept them as a step.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Hoppe argues democratic governments spend and borrow to buy votes, and adherents reject state stimulus altogether.

economic-freedom.rationale: Private property and free markets are treated as the base of every other freedom.

force-without-un.rationale: State war-making is rejected whether or not a body approves it.

dominated-front.rationale: Blocs of states are further states and the ideology does not organize politics by geopolitics.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Rothbard holds that the state has no right to regulate private life and favors the equal right of each to self-ownership.

ban-interest.rationale: Voluntary lending at interest is a lawful contract, though Rothbard and Tucker disagreed over how interest arises.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Force may be used only against aggression, so a law separating races uses force against peaceful people.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rothbard described the state as organized banditry that benefits those who capture it, though not in Marxist terms.

elite-replacement.rationale: Hoppe argues democratic rulers import voters for gain, but the ideology does not endorse a deliberate replacement plot.

proportional-representation.rationale: Adherents regard democratic institutions as illegitimate whatever the electoral system, so it is a matter of indifference.

national-mission.rationale: State attempts to spread a government abroad are war and aggression.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Rothbard holds that the state is the main structure of coercion, and the mainstream does not see systemic male advantage; left strands differ.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Rothbard opposes compulsory birth control, and state eugenics would use force on peaceful people.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Rothbard holds judges and police would have no special immunity, so those who commit abuses would be held liable like anyone else.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Minarchism is rejected as inconsistent because it still relies on compulsory funding.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Sexual and family life are private, and no one may be coerced over them.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Judges and police would have no special rights to coerce beyond others, and rights are held equally by all, but equality of outcomes is rejected.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Rothbard's approach based on homesteading and return of stolen property gives no settled answer on a general claim.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The ideology favors competing private legal systems chosen by contract, not one uniform law.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Force may be used only against aggression, and slaughtering one's own property is not.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The ideology holds only voluntary individual consent legitimizes authority, though it denies that majority consent binds anyone.

population-transfer.rationale: Rothbard says no physical force may be used against anyone not convicted as a criminal.

state-harmful.rationale: Abolishing the state, a coercive monopoly that Rothbard says is organized banditry, is the defining aim.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Hoppe argues that democratic rulers buy votes and favor short-term gain at the expense of the public, and Rothbard treats officials as beneficiaries of state power.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The non-aggression principle, that force may be used only against force, is the foundation of the ideology.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists want no state to begin with and oppose using state power against peaceful political expression.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Their liberty is the negative one of freedom from actual aggression against person and property, not freedom from unused power.

separated-powers.rationale: They regard constitutional checks as having failed to constrain the state and want competing private providers instead of divided state branches.

vanguard-party.rationale: Their individualist, voluntarist approach rejects disciplined leading parties and revolutionary elites.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Equal property rights and the rejection of redistribution mean policy gives no first claim to the poor.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Hoppe stresses cultural homogeneity while other adherents reject that view, so the strand is split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The state and its offices are to be abolished in favor of private provision, so filling public offices by any method is beside the point and rejected.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rothbard insists on no special immunity for rulers and no force against the unconvicted, which rules out suspending protections.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price ceilings are state coercion over voluntary exchange and are held to cause shortages.

party-commands-army.rationale: The state and its armed forces are to be abolished, and Rothbard calls conscription enslavement.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Adherents split on immigration and the state citizenship is a creature of, so there is no settled position (per this audit's scope).

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Officials in a state are paid from taxation, which adherents see as theft; they would prefer little pay but have no stated position on a wage cap.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Rothbardian anarchists reject involuntary hierarchy and compulsory state churches; private churches could be run by anyone, but a national church governed from above is rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Rothbard calls war state mass murder, and adherents oppose supporting their own state in war; defeat is welcomed more than loyalty, though not all endorse working for it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The non-aggression principle forbids force against peaceful speech and art, so state censorship is rejected.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Rothbard treats war as mass murder by the state and opposes foreign entanglements, so ending alliances and bringing troops home follows directly.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Private ownership and freedom of contract are central, so forbidding renting would violate property rights.

people-in-arms.rationale: They oppose the standing army and favour private defence, and back an armed population, but through market firms rather than a citizen militia; adherents differ.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The tradition has no stance on education and rural-urban reality; adherents are divided.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Adherents split on culture, from Hoppe's defence of cultural ranking to left-Rothbardians; set neutral.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Rothbard opposes laws against consensual acts between adults; force may be used only to combat force.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: No state, so no state citizenship; Hoppe favours restrictive private borders while others favour open ones; adherents split.

minority-language-support.rationale: Taxation is theft, so state-funded teaching, services and ballots in minority languages would go; languages are private matters.

religious-exemptions.rationale: They reject coercive general law but a legal exemption for some is not a goal; no clear stance.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberty and the non-aggression principle are the foundation of the theory, which allows no trade of freedom for growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Rothbard holds that taxation is theft, so any duty to aid the poor is moral and voluntary rather than enforced.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Adherents see state armies and weapons as tools of mass murder funded by theft, and would have defence provided privately.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property acquired by labor and self-ownership is the basis of the theory, and owners may use it as they wish short of aggression.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Government restriction on mere risk would be coercion against peaceful people; adherents would handle harm through private property and tort liability once harm is shown.

collective-defense.rationale: Rothbard condemns state militaries and wars as mass murder, and treaty-bound state alliances are tools of such wars.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The ideology abolishes the state and so has no head of state to be non-partisan; Hoppe prefers monarchy to democracy but few adherents follow.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Secession is welcomed down to the individual level, and military force against peaceful separation is aggression the non-aggression principle forbids.

character-from-environment.rationale: The ideology rests on self-ownership and individual choice and has no common doctrine on nature versus nurture; adherents split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rothbard insists that no one, including officials, enjoys special immunity from the law and the non-aggression principle.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Any constitution assumes a state, which the ideology rejects in favor of voluntary market arrangements.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists reject Marxist class theory and socialism entirely, so the question's premises are not accepted.

land-redistribution.rationale: Property acquired by labor and homesteading is inviolable, so forced transfer of land is theft.

refugee-return.rationale: Adherents tie return to the legitimacy of property claims and voluntary arrangements, and split on the principle.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The non-aggression principle and rejection of the state rule out territorial claims by states on ethnic grounds.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Rothbard's personal-liberty position holds that victimless acts should not be punished.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dress laws are coercion of peaceful conduct, which the non-aggression principle forbids.

common-currency.rationale: Adherents prefer private competing money, typically commodity-based, to any state-managed currency, whether national or multinational.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Adherents favour voluntary private institutions for any group, but the statement frames it within the state, which they do not accept as legitimate; split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Property and voluntary association, not collective strategy, guide their view; no standard position.

ban-cartels.rationale: They reject antitrust law as state interference and regard state privilege, not voluntary market concentration, as the source of monopoly power.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are taxpayer-funded transfers, which anarcho-capitalists regard as theft.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Hoppe and others reject democracy and majority rule as a source of legitimate authority.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Mandated representation is state coercion, and they hold that public bodies should not exist or should be chosen voluntarily.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: They advocate free trade, so a closed bloc is opposed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Market pricing and material incentives are central to their economics, so replacing them by moral incentives is rejected.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: They aim at ideas-driven change and market alternatives rather than armed vanguards, though they accept defensive force.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rothbard treats rule by a state over others as aggression and war as mass murder, so imperial tutelage has no justification.

patriotic-education.rationale: Loyalty to the nation and its symbols is loyalty to the state, which the ideology wants abolished, and it opposes state-run schooling.

former-empire-influence.rationale: State pursuit of influence abroad is seen as aggression funded by taxation, so adherents reject it.

delink-world-market.rationale: Adherents favor free trade and voluntary exchange across borders and see no gain from cutting ties.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Property owners are held to decide whom they deal with, so anti-discrimination law is a violation of property rights.

elective-rulers.rationale: Hoppe argues private monarchy is preferable to democracy; ancaps reject state rule altogether.

minority-veto.rationale: Voluntarism holds that no person is bound without consent; the non-aggression principle forbids imposing decisions on dissenters.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Rothbard denied rights to animals, treating them as property; some adherents differ.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: They reject foreign aid as state transfer but welcome private trade and investment, so adherents are split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Adherents are split between a slavery-centred and a centralisation-and-tariffs revisionist reading.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Anarcho-capitalism abolishes the state and its armed forces, so a political role is rejected.

office-by-exam.rationale: Government posts are to be abolished or privatised, and the question presumes a state bureaucracy; examination-chosen officials are not favoured over market provision.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Voluntary sales of private property to any buyer are protected, and the state has no right to interfere with them.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: They want the state pension system abolished in favour of private, voluntary provision; individual private accounts are the closer of the two options.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land acquired by homesteading and trade is fully owned and may be sold, left idle or bequeathed; use-based tenure is rejected.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Taxation is theft and the state should not exist, so approving its budget is not the fix; legislative control is at best preferable to none.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Property owners may sell to anyone, and a state ban on foreign buyers violates owners' rights, though Hoppe's strand is more restrictive on immigration.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Liability for outcomes regardless of intent compels association and punishes people without aggression, which the non-aggression principle forbids.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Free-market economics treats consumer choices as the individual's own business and consumption as the aim of production, so the claim that it does more harm than good is rejected.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: War and its financing by taxation are condemned as mass murder and theft, so funding foreign armed groups is rejected.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Rothbard calls state war mass murder and the state an aggressor, so invading an ally by force is condemned.

corporate-influence.rationale: Rothbardians condemn state-business collusion and privilege, though they would end it by abolishing the state rather than regulating lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Voluntary exchange and association are central; state limits on who may fund whom violate property and contract rights.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Tax-funded subsidies are theft in this view and the state should not direct family choices.

residents-only-property.rationale: Owners should decide who to sell to; Hoppe favours private covenant communities, but local authorities lack that right.

job-guarantee.rationale: Taxation to fund state employment is theft and distorts the market, so it is opposed.

democratic-peace.rationale: Hoppe argues democracy is no better than monarchy, and spreading it by state action is opposed.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The state is a coercive monopoly and law has no moral authority merely as law; this follows from the non-aggression principle.

non-intervention.rationale: Rothbardians oppose foreign wars and interventions, though they deny states have rights in the first place.

local-production.rationale: They favour free trade and market choice over mandated localism, though people may choose local goods.

national-law-over-international.rationale: They reject state authority at both levels, so neither takes precedence.

religious-nation.rationale: Nations as political units are rejected and communities form by voluntary association, not creed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists defend private ownership of industry, land and capital as the product of labor and voluntary exchange, and reject common ownership of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Rothbard was a fierce critic of communism but also of war and conscription as state mass murder, so adherents split between defeating it and peaceful non-intervention.

religion-illusion.rationale: Many adherents, Rothbard among them, were irreligious while others are religious traditionalists; the ideology as such takes no position and rejects the materialist account of religion fading.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Adherents credit free-market capitalism with creating prosperity and see it as the engine of material progress, while rejecting its state-linked distortions.

socialized-care.rationale: Public services funded by taxation are rejected; childcare and housework are left to families and voluntary private arrangements.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Voluntary communes are permitted in a free society, but a program to reorganise society into common-property communities is not the ideology, which defends private property.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Adherents regard free-market capitalism, with private property and no state, as the sound basis for society and reject both communism and a middle path.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The mainstream Rothbardian strand has no denialist doctrine and condemns state mass murder; denial is a fringe position, so the typical adherent disagrees.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Rothbard argues that consensual sex between adults is outside the law's proper reach and that sex laws violate liberty.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The non-aggression principle forbids using force against peaceful dissent and association, and anarcho-capitalists reject the state that would do the suppressing.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Punishing speech or religious practice is aggression against peaceful persons under the non-aggression principle, and the theory leaves no role for state enforcement of religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists oppose the state and its imperial adventures as plunder funded by taxation, so governing colonies for the ruler's benefit is rejected.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: This is a religious duty and not a libertarian principle; anarcho-capitalists allow self-defence as an individual right but reject any obligation imposed on every member of a faith.

alienated-labor.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists accept wage labor and private ownership of industry as voluntary exchange and reject the Marxist account of alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The mainstream strand judges people as individuals and defends peaceful voluntary association, so it rejects blanket claims about a religion; some adherents who follow Hoppe on culture differ.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists deny that political authority is legitimate at all, and ground rights in self-ownership rather than in God or the people.

social-market-economy.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists reject both state regulation and welfare provision and want a fully free market with no state.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: They want the state's military abolished and defense supplied by competing private firms, so the national army is abolished though armed defense continues.

rich-first.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists accept unequal outcomes from voluntary exchange and reject state management of who gets rich, but the slogan is Deng-era Chinese policy and not their own; adherents would neither endorse nor oppose it.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists oppose state wars and alliances as plunder and mass murder, and a non-interventionist stance is a consequence of rejecting the state.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: They defend interest as the market price of time preference and want banking left to profit-seeking private firms.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not a theme of the Rothbardian strand; their private-property view of nature and individualism make them reject the claim, an inference from principle.

reification.rationale: They defend markets as the voluntary exchanges of individuals, and the claim that markets distort social relations is the critics' view they reject.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: They hold that property rights, including in presses and halls, are the basis of free speech (Rothbard on property rights and speech).

racial-franchise.rationale: They are individualists who reject racial collectivism and, in principle, the state franchise; Rothbard criticised racial discrimination by law.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Rothbard's personal-liberty view opposes laws against victimless acts, including limits on adult marriage.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Rothbardians hold that wealth earned or exchanged voluntarily is legitimate and that liberty is threatened only by force, which is the state's tool.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: They reject any state schooling or state-enforced belief; religion is a private choice.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Rothbard would replace state police and prisons with competing private protectors and restitution to victims, though not with community care.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Voluntary charity and private mutual aid are held to replace the welfare state, which is condemned as funded by theft.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious bodies are private associations free to set their own rules, so adherents would not impose either rule; they are split in views.

rent-control.rationale: Price controls interfere with voluntary contracts and property, which the ideology treats as inviolable.

abolish-ip.rationale: Most modern adherents, such as Kinsella, reject intellectual property, and Rothbard opposed state-defined monopolies on ideas.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Property owners' returns are legitimate under the labor and self-ownership theory, and they accept private ownership of industry.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Rothbard holds that force is permitted to combat force, so defence of self and others is legitimate.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Voluntary exchange and property by acquisition leave no role for ethnic claims on economic life.

independent-unions.rationale: Unions are voluntary associations that should answer to members; with no state, there is no state or party to control them.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Rothbard would privatise all services, including police, courts and utilities, leaving none in public hands.

municipal-property.rationale: Private property in the means of production is the core principle; community or state ownership is rejected.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Rothbard calls taxation theft, so government funding of research is rejected, though private ageing research is welcomed.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Taxation is theft and the state has no rightful power to trace or block payments; adherents such as the agorists favour untraceable money.

person-over-state.rationale: Rothbard holds self-ownership absolute: conscription is slavery and no person may be used as a means by the state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The ideology is silent on spiritual nature; adherents range from religious to atheist, so they split.

dense-cities.rationale: Land use is left to private choice and prices; adherents do not hold a view on which form is better for the environment.

racial-pride.rationale: Adherents are split: individualists see race as irrelevant, while Hoppe-aligned paleolibertarians are more sympathetic.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Rothbard condemns war as mass murder and holds force legitimate only in defence, though anarcho-capitalists do not support state armies.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists reject the nation-state and see voluntary association as the basis of community, but some adherents such as Hoppe stress cultural and national ties.

communal-electorates.rationale: They reject the state and democracy itself; Hoppe's critique of democracy rules out electorates of any kind.

free-public-college.rationale: They would privatise education and oppose tax-funded services, so tuition-free public colleges are rejected.

pollution-taxes.rationale: They treat pollution as a violation of property rights to be handled by private courts and liability, not by state taxes.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists want defense and policing supplied by competing private agencies, so a state monopoly on arms is the very thing they reject.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax-funded income top-ups are redistribution through compulsory taxation, which adherents regard as theft.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Adherents oppose state borrowing but reject the state as the enforcer of its own limits, so a legal rule is neither clearly welcome nor clearly rejected.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The goal is abolition of the state rather than capturing it, though adherents favor mainly peaceful and market means over seizure of power.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Polycentric private law lets communities choose rules, yet adherents hold that property-based market exchange is the only just order, so they are split on 'no fixed blueprint'.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Cancelling loans means shifting costs to taxpayers or lenders by state action, and adherents hold contracts must be honored.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Rothbard grounds rights in natural law derived from human nature, though adherents have no concern with 'redesign' as such.

public-service-media.rationale: Tax-funded broadcasters are state institutions, which adherents would abolish or privatize.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Adherents hold varied religious or secular views and the ideology is silent on whether religions share one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Price supports and state credit are redistribution funded by taxation, which Rothbard treats as theft; farming would be left to the market.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The ideology has no position on how languages are named or divided.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Rothbard-style law treats pollution as trespass against property, remedied by restitution and injunctions in private courts rather than by agencies.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Individual liberty and property are the ruling principle, so restricting freedoms for environmental goals is rejected.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Employment is voluntary contract for anarcho-capitalists, so no one can be forced to join or pay a union; stated in the overview of their principles.

voter-id.rationale: They reject the state's legitimacy and care little about how its elections are run, so adherents have no settled view.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: With no state, no religious interpretation could have legal precedence; Rothbard's force-only-against-force rule forbids imposing belief.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Hoppe argues democracy is not a legitimate check on the state, and anarcho-capitalists judge governments by their coercion, not their selection.

premarital-sex.rationale: Rothbard argues sex between consenting adults must be free of legal interference.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Cutting access is initiating force against people and property, which Rothbard rules out.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Rothbard rejects tax-funded welfare, though Friedman-style adherents accept a negative income tax as a step toward abolition; adherents split toward disagreement.

race-social-construct.rationale: Adherents split between those who dismiss racial categories and those, like some Hoppe followers, who do not.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Tax-funded state agencies rest on taxation, which Rothbard calls theft.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Rothbardian property theory grounds ownership in first use and labor-mixing of unowned resources, as the reference article on the ideology describes.

national-church-status.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists oppose any state privilege and want religion to be wholly voluntary, so a legally privileged church is rejected.

equal-conscription.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists treat conscription as slavery and oppose it for everyone, so the 'neither' branch of the statement applies.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Rothbard holds that force may be used only against those proven to have initiated force, with trials in private courts.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Property comes from homesteading by labour, and users owe no compensation to society; only geolibertarian dissenters differ.

self-ownership.rationale: Anarcho-capitalism is described as resting on self-ownership as a foundational principle.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists call taxation theft and want all taxes abolished, which includes consumption taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: State welfare of any kind is rejected; if help is given it is voluntary charity aimed at need, so the state-run choice is not endorsed.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists oppose state subsidies, licences and protections as coercive favours that distort the market.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Anarcho-capitalism favours technology but has no stated view on reviving ancestral values; adherents such as Hoppe differ from others.

national-resource-control.rationale: Resources should be privately owned, not under national control, which anarcho-capitalists see as state ownership.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Rothbardian theory judges justice by whether property was acquired by labour and exchanged without force, not by the resulting pattern.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Adherents split on race and culture, and the sources do not settle this statement.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Rothbard contrasts natural law with state-made law, and the abolition of state courts rests on the view that coercive statutes carry no moral authority.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The Austrian-influenced theory grounds value in subjective preference and treats wage labour as voluntary exchange, not in labour.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: They reject the state and socialism alike, and a party-ruled economy is the kind of state power they would abolish.

missingStatements.text: It is always wrong to initiate force against another person or their property, whatever the goal.
missingStatements.rationale: The non-aggression principle is the foundation of the theory, and Rothbard says force may be used only to combat force.

missingStatements.text: Patents and copyrights should be abolished.
missingStatements.rationale: Most modern adherents (Kinsella) reject intellectual property, and Rothbard opposed government-defined terms.
missingStatements.declined: A secondary position on which adherents split and which most other ideologies would not take a side on; not defining enough to be answered in every audit.

notes: Anarchists generally reject the label as incompatible with capitalism. Adherents split on immigration, cultural conservatism, abortion, intellectual property and whether law needs a shared ethic (Rothbard) or not (Friedman).
